newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end lower, overall market weak.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end lower, overall market weak.

text.p: Singapore shares finished lower on Monday as the overall market softened in the wake of weak results and the absence of incentives to trade on, brokers said.
After last week's run-up, second board stocks fell the heaviest fall, dropping 1.67 points, or 2.08 percent, to 78.59 on the UOB SESDAQ index.

Blue chips followed with the UOB Blue Chip index falling 10.74 points, or 1.15 percent, to 923.96. Though the market has discounted the downgrading, the Morgan Stanley Capital Index (MSCI) is expected to underweigh Singapore stocks this week.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index dropped 24.74 points to 2,128.80.
The bearish market was reflected in the number of losers swamping gainers -- 260 to 62 -- and a thin market volume of 62.93 million shares.
Malaysia's Kemayan Corp was the most active with 3.25 million shares traded after its parent company reported a 17 percent increase in its annual net profits. It rose S$0.01 to S$1.81.
Cycle & Carriage and Singapore Press foreign were among the losers, each falling S$0.50 to S$13.00 and S$23.90 respectively.
